I have farmed in Quzhou County my whole life. My father taught me how to work this land, and I have never gone to school. I cannot read or write, but I know the seasons and the soil. I farm about 10 mu of land.

This year, I will do what my neighbors and I have always done. I will plant winter wheat on 7 mu in October, right after the National Day holiday. Wheat is our staple — it feeds my family and the straw goes to the animals. I will buy improved wheat seeds from the agro-store because they grow better than the seeds I save myself. Before sowing, I will rotary till the field to loosen the soil. I will spread compound fertilizer as a base and then topdress with urea in the spring when the wheat greens up. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at green-up, and once when the grain is filling. I will spray four times for aphids and weeds.

In early June, right after the wheat harvest, I will plant maize on those same 7 mu. I will buy hybrid maize seeds — they grow fast and give a good yield. I will not till the soil for maize; I will sow straight into the wheat stubble to save time, diesel, and labor. Maize grows through the hot summer, and I will irrigate it twice when the rain is not enough. I will spray a few times for insects and weeds. The maize should be ready by October.

On my other 3 mu, I will plant cotton in April. Cotton is hard work — it needs many sprays for bollworms — but it brings cash money that I need for my family. I will rotary till the cotton plot and plant improved cotton seeds. I will irrigate twice and spray whenever I see pests.

I do not use computers or read books. I watch the sky, I talk to the old farmers in my village, and I stick to what has always worked.
